clue.text: Bone from bird held by father

indicators.note: something held by another sits inside its grip, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
the large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: Someone retrieving a bone from a bird that their father is holding.
explanation.walkthrough: Fr is the standard abbreviation for a priest's title, Father.
explanation.definitionFit: The femur is the thigh bone, the longest in the human skeleton.

clue.text: Pictures covering journey, to be projected separately

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece covering another sits above it

parts.note: the pictures are films, as in going to the pictures
a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: A set of slides of a holiday journey to be shown on a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: something whose frames are each shown on their own.
explanation.definitionFit: A filmstrip is a strip of still images shown one frame at a time through a projector.

clue.text: Sort of square repast outside for copper, say

indicators.note: the meal word sits outside, wrapping around the square piece

parts.note: a repast is a meal
a T-square is a drawing instrument, so T is a sort of square

explanation.surface: A proper hearty meal bought for a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: A square meal is a hearty one, but 'square' splits off with 'Sort of'. Copper is also British slang for a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is an example of a metal, the 'say' marking it as one instance.

clue.text: Tear off below right-hand page in clergyman's office

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece below another is written after it

parts.note: the recto is the right-hand page of an open book
to rate is to scold, as in tearing someone off a strip

explanation.surface: Someone ripping something off beneath a page in a vicar's study.
explanation.walkthrough: To tear someone off a strip is British for to tell them off; rate is an old verb for berate.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectorate is the post or tenure of a rector, a parish clergyman.

clue.text: Utter space of a private cabin!

parts.note: to state is to utter or declare
room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: An exclamation at how cramped, or how spacious, a private cabin on board is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective (utter space, total void) but works as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A stateroom is the term for a passenger's private sleeping quarters on a ship.

clue.text: Two-point mains adaptor needed for Japanese guitar

indicators.note: an adaptor changes one form into another, so the letters are adapted into a new order

parts.note: two compass points, south and east
taken as written

explanation.surface: A two-pin plug adaptor needed to plug in an electric Japanese guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two-point' suggests a two-pin plug, but it is two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: The samisen is a three-stringed Japanese lute, loosely described as a guitar.

clue.text: An associate member of RADA for example

parts.note: the indefinite article
a crony is a close companion or associate
M is the abbreviation for member, as in MP

explanation.surface: Someone who is an associate member of the drama school.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, London's famous drama school, pronounced as a word from its initials.
explanation.definitionFit: RADA is pronounced as a word formed from initial letters, which makes it an example of that kind of abbreviation.

clue.text: Hand light for each one

parts.note: East is one of the four hands at bridge
a Very light is a coloured signal flare fired from a pistol

explanation.surface: A torch or lamp handed out to everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players (hands) are North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: Every means each one of a group without exception, all individually.

clue.text: Look up works relating to nasal function

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look, as in lo and behold
a works is a factory

explanation.surface: An instruction to research writings about how the nose works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look up' reads as research, but the up turns lo round.
explanation.definitionFit: Olfactory means concerned with the sense of smell, which the nose performs.

clue.text: A certain person in Montana was a painter

indicators.note: being in something places one piece inside the other

parts.note: MT is the postal abbreviation for Montana
one, as in one might say, means a certain person

explanation.surface: A local claim that someone in Montana used to paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet was the French Impressionist artist famous for his water lilies.

clue.text: One who appears behind?

parts.note: surface reading: someone seen at the rear, perhaps a person showing their backside
setter's reading: someone who turns up behind time, after the agreed hour

explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' suggests position or a rear end; here it means behind schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A person arriving after others, or after the start, is one who turns up behind time.

clue.text: Impish piece of self-indulgence

indicators.note: a piece is only a part, so the letters come from inside the following phrase

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the two halves of the hyphenated word

explanation.surface: Mischievous behaviour described as a little bit of self-indulgence.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in self-indulgence is ignored; the letters run across it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means like an elf, and elves are mischievous, puckish little sprites.

clue.text: Round of applause with reservation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a burst of cheering or clapping
second meaning: a saving clause or mental proviso, an older sense of the word

explanation.surface: An audience that claps but holds something back.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense, from Latin salvo jure (saving the right), is a proviso or excuse.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a simultaneous burst of fire or cheering and, in an older sense, a saving proviso.

clue.text: Does one tack on a strand?-

definitions.text: Does one tack on a strand?

parts.words: Does one tack on a strand?
parts.note: surface reading: someone pinning or stitching onto a thread or strand of hair
setter's reading: tack means change course into the wind, and a strand is a beach

explanation.walkthrough: Strand is an old word for a beach, and tacking is a sailing manoeuvre; the craft sails on sand on wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: A sand yacht is a wheeled sailing vehicle driven by wind along flat beaches.

clue.text: Go back to school and take shower after soak

indicators.note: coming after means the second idea is placed later in the word than the first

parts.note: to ret is to soak flax or hemp to soften it
a shower is rain, and to rain is to take the form of a shower

explanation.surface: Someone back at school having to shower after getting soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: RET is a specialist word for soaking plant stems to loosen the fibres.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrain is to learn new skills again, returning to study as if to school.

clue.text: Ditch insect biting

parts.note: a trench is a ditch
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: An insect in a ditch that bites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Biting' seems to describe the insect, but it is the definition, in the sense of sharp or cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant describes incisive, cutting remarks, figuratively sharp just like biting criticism.

clue.text: Guy blends fruit for pickling

parts.note: a guy is a man
goes as in harmonises: the colours go well together

explanation.surface: A cook mixing fruit to make chutney or pickle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blends' looks like a kitchen verb but means matches, as colours go together.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangoes, often unripe, are the basis of mango pickle and chutney in Indian cooking.

clue.text: Does she await the first issue of Luna, April edition?

definitions.text: Does she await the first issue

indicators.note: an edition is a new version, so the letters appear in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A query whether someone is waiting for the first number of a magazine called Luna, April edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' reads as a magazine number; it means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: A nullipara is the medical term for a woman who has never given birth, so her first child is still to come.

clue.text: Dermatologist's test made without warning

definitions.meaning: first meaning, playful: a skin doctor examining a pimple or blemish
second meaning: a random inspection carried out unannounced

explanation.surface: A skin specialist springing a surprise examination on a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: The word test is shared by both readings; the first is whimsical, resting on a spot being a pimple.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a random unannounced inspection, and literally a doctor examining a blemish on the skin.

clue.text: See and post letters for Elizabeth Barrett Browning, say

indicators.note: the letters of the words are taken out and laid down afresh in another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to read and send letters on behalf of a famous Victorian writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' simply joins the two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth Barrett Browning was a celebrated Victorian female poet, an example of the older term.

clue.text: Impresario calling for silence putting on foreign woman.

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting one thing on another stacks it on top

parts.note: sh is the sound made to call for quiet

indicators.note: something foreign is strange and unfamiliar, so the letters are put into an unfamiliar order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatre producer hushing the room before presenting a foreign leading lady.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresario organises entertainments, a showman who stages spectacles with flair.

clue.text: Call to meet people?

parts.note: surface reading: a summons to go and get to know some people
setter's reading: the meet is a gathering of a fox hunt, so meet people are the hunt followers

explanation.walkthrough: In British fox hunting the meet is the assembly of riders and hounds; this is the cry given when the fox is sighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Tally-ho is the huntsman's traditional shout to the riders and hounds on spotting the quarry.

clue.text: Sort prepared to be a compositor

parts.note: a type is a sort or kind
set means ready, prepared

explanation.surface: Someone sorted and ready to start work as a printer's compositor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort' is also a printer's word for a piece of type, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A compositor arranges type for printing, which is exactly the work of setting type.

clue.text: In high spirits, stand up before a band

indicators.note: coming before places the first idea ahead of the rest in the word

parts.note: to cock is to make stand up, as a dog cocks its ears
taken as written
a hoop is a circular band, as on a barrel

explanation.surface: Someone so elated they stand up in front of a musical group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks musical but is a ring of metal or wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Cock-a-hoop is an idiom for exultant, boastfully delighted.

clue.text: Go up to Conservative member

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a member is a limb, an arm or leg

explanation.surface: Someone approaching a Tory MP, or rising up to their rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests an MP, but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb is to ascend, to move upward.

clue.text: Got up like an English circumnavigator

parts.note: the indefinite article
Sir Alec Rose sailed single-handed round the world in 1967 to 1968

explanation.surface: Someone who rose early, as a round-the-world sailor would.
explanation.walkthrough: Alec Rose was a Portsmouth greengrocer knighted for his solo voyage round the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Arose is the past tense of arise, meaning stood up or got out of bed.

clue.text: First signs of it looking irregular? Any cramp in the lower body?

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter, so only initials are kept

parts.note: the initial letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: A worried question about an odd-looking body part and a cramp in the lower abdomen.
explanation.definitionFit: Iliac describes the ilium, the hip bone, and the region of the lower abdomen around it.

clue.text: Popular aid programme for the republic

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: a programme sets things out in a planned order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A popular overseas aid scheme for a developing nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aid programme' reads as development help; programme is the rearranging signal.
explanation.definitionFit: India became a republic in 1950, the country of over a billion people in South Asia.

clue.text: State in which I had retired with nothing

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the word for had is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
O looks like a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone describing the American state they retired to with no money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' looks like stopping work but turns the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the north-west.

clue.text: Make a hash of Delhi man's ingredients

indicators.note: ingredients are mixed together in cooking, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A cook botching a curry by spoiling an Indian man's ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a hash of' sounds like cooking but means bungle.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a hash of something is an idiom for botching it, handling it badly.

clue.text: American tree with flatter top

parts.note: to butter someone up is to flatter them; a flatterer is one who butters
the nut is slang for the head, the top of the body

explanation.surface: A tree with a flatter crown than others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flatter' reads as more flat, but it is the verb to flatter, i.e. butter.
explanation.definitionFit: The butternut is a North American walnut species, also called white walnut.

clue.text: A deficiency? Oh, dear!

parts.note: taken as written
a lack is a shortage

explanation.surface: A groan of dismay at discovering a shortfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Alack is an archaic exclamation of sorrow or regret, as in alas and alack.
